title.narrative: Technical assistance to MOHCC to implement HRF (II)

description.narrative:
A continuation of technical assistance to MOHCC to implement the Health Resilience Fund (HRD, 2022-2025) - amendment of contract to extend 12 months,

The overall objective of this technical assistance is to assist the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC) implement the new Health Resilience Fund (HRF) by increasing coordination and improving transparency and accountability

In line with the implementation of the MIP (2021-2017), the Action Document ¿Improving Health Outcomes for the Population of Zimbabwe (Health Resilience Fund, HRF) (number: NDICI AFRICA/2022/43392)¿ aims to continue to strengthen primary health care (PHC) structures, and enhance health security measures, in order to protect the population against the main health threats i.e. a continuation of the EU supported Health Development Fund(HDF) 2016-2021 i.e. the Health Resilience Fund (HRF) November 2022 to December 2025). The total amount of the EU contribution is EUR 41 000 000 and will be executed through indirect management with UNICEF. The Action supports the implementation of a realistic Exit Strategy aimed at enhancing the government¿s capacity to fund and manage health services at primary level after the end of EU support.    As the new HRF will start on in November 2022 ( retrospective financing to 1 July 2022) , technical assistance is    needed as soon as possible after this date as a new Programme Management and Performance Unit (PMU) will be set up within the MoHCC to implement the project inNovember 2022. 

Apart from ongoing activities as detailed in the current contract, additional TA will be needed for the following additional activities:

1. Co-ordinating the new Team in the Programme Management Unit (PMU), MoHCC

2. Developing a realistic roadmap for the MOHCC to exit from the HRF.

3. The need for the PMU to assist the implementing partners in reporting on the progress of the HRF

 4. Technical assistance to set up a National Public Health Institute (NPHI).

In light of the above circumstances, which were unforeseen and beyond the control of the contracting authority and in light of the importance of the Health Resilience Fund project for the EUD, it is imperative to amend the current contract. As per provisions, this amendment allows for an addition of up to 50% of the initial contract value. The amendment is not only justified but is essential to ensure continuity of technical assistance to the MOHCC.
